title: Signal titles must not embed run-specific identifiers; dedup key should normalise before matching
description: Signals whose titles include specific UUIDs, signal IDs, run IDs, timestamps, or file paths generate a new catalogue entry on every invocation rather than incrementing an existing pattern signal. The dedup procedure uses exact title + category matching, so an embedded UUID makes each instance unique — even when the root cause, category, and resolution are identical. Multiple per-instance signals accumulate without ever elevating the underlying pattern signal. Two complementary fixes are needed: a skill-level title discipline rule and a dedup-level normalisation step.
proposed_resolution: 1. Add a 'Signal title discipline' rule to the QA Architect persona and the Canonical Signal Dedup-and-Write Procedure: titles must describe the error pattern, not name specific UUIDs, run IDs, signal IDs, or file paths — those belong in the description field. 2. Add a normalise_title step to the dedup identity-key computation that strips UUID-shaped tokens (8-4-4-4-12 hex), ISO 8601 timestamps, and filesystem paths before matching against the index, providing a fallback guard against future title-discipline violations.
